annotations.title: Write a month of video ideas

description: Start a content calendar for a topic: count faceless videos (1-31) over days (7-31), each with a title, hook, the exact script, caption, hashtags and a posting time. Best: write the ideas yourself in the conversation and send them as items (taken as written, at once); otherwise Clypmint writes them (this call keeps going until they are written, or tells you to call again with the same operation_id). Makes nothing and spends nothing; answers plan_id, the ideas and the quote (credits a video, room left this month). Show the user the ideas, change them with edit_content_plan, and approve_plan only after their yes. Use for "start a faceless account" or "a month of posts about X". Cost: Free to write; making each video costs about 4 credits (30 s).

count.description: How many videos (1-31); leave out when sending items.

items.description: Ideas you wrote yourself (title, hook, script, caption, hashtags): taken as written, at once. Without them Clypmint writes the ideas.
One word, letters, digits or _, with or without #.

script.description: The exact words the narrator reads, about 2.5 words a second of video.

operation_id.description: A stable ID for this request. Preserve it on retries. Use a new ID only for a deliberate new request.

platforms.description: Where each post goes; Instagram when left out.

start_at.description: The first day; tomorrow when left out.

voice.description: The narrator for a video made from words: matilda, sarah, jessica, alice, liam, chris, brian, george, roger, laura, charlie, river, will, eric, bella, daniel, lily, bill, adam, callum, harry (sarah: calm, reassuring, health and money; alice: a clear British educator; brian: deep documentary; liam: energetic ads). Leave out to let Clypmint pick one that fits the words. "Voice: <name>" in instructions does the same.

name: plan_content

outputSchema.description: Clypmint plan_content result. Error results carry error; successful requests expose the identifiers and state available for the next step. Signed media stays in private metadata.
